licenses.text:
American Standard Version Byzantine Text, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/engasvbt/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's page for this
translation):
> "American Standard Version Byzantine Text
The Holy Bible with Apocrypha, American Standard Version conformed to the Byzantine Text New Testament
Public Domain
Language: English
Dialect: Archaic American

Changes to the ASV dedicated to the Public Domain by Adam Boyd in 2021. The ASV itself is in the Public Domain due to copyright expiration."

Why this is public domain:
The American Standard Version (1901) is public domain in the United States (its country of origin) through copyright expiration. The changes that form this edition were dedicated to the public domain by Adam Boyd in 2021, as eBible.org's page states; a dedication of this kind applies everywhere. Admitted as an exception on the maintainer's decision alone (2026-10-21): the only public-domain statement for Robert Adam Boyd's changes is eBible.org's label, and eBible.org is not Boyd's project; the same exception covers his three editions on eBible.org (engasvbt, englxxup, grctr).

The read-aloud archive holds the Bible text chapter by chapter as plain
text, a front file, the copyright page (copr.htm, left out of the source),
and eBible.org's signing key (keys.asc, left out).

Sources of these facts: eBible.org's details page
(https://ebible.org/details.php?id=engasvbt) and the edition's own files.

held_out_by.note: eBible's chapter files, <code>_<NNN>_<BOOK>_<CC>_read.txt, are held out by book and chapter, so the same chapter is held out in every translation at once (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23)

decision.reason: exception on the maintainer's decision alone: Robert Adam Boyd's changes rest on eBible.org's label, not on his own words

note: eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside, so a rebuild with the same text still matches.
